title: add vpc control plane provisioning: subnets, interface endpoints, sgs, peering, route53
author: Aisha Khan
description: Context and motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private require a production-ready VPC control plane with multi-AZ subnets, secure interface endpoints for AWS services, explicit security groups for control-plane traffic, cross-account VPC peering support, and Route53 private hosted zone peering. This PR adds a reusable Terraform module, Helm values/templates and installer upgrade hooks to provision and manage those resources declaratively. Scope: - Terraform module: terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane - Supports multi-AZ subnet provisioning (public/private for control plane workloads), ENI tagging, configurable CIDR blocks, and default route tables. - Interface endpoints: SSM, SSM-Messaging, EC2, ECR (api and docker), STS, KMS optional, and S3 gateway endpoints where appropriate. - Security groups: least-privilege default SG for control-plane nodes, egress-only rules for metadata and endpoints, and a separate SG for peering endpoints. - Peering: cross-account peering support with automated route table propagation hooks and optional acceptor role. - DNS: Route53 private hosted zone creation and peering to customer VPCs with validation step and optional delegated subdomain config. - Helm and installer: new values schema and templates to consume the provisioned resources, upgrade/rollback hooks to handle drift-safe migrations, and a k8s Job for DNS validation post-provisioning. Motivation: Bring private installer to parity with enterprise network requirements and make upgrades predictable and reversible. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implemented and documented - [x] Helm values and templates updated - [x] Upgrade/rollback hooks implemented - [x] Integration tests for provisioning in CI - [x] Documentation for operator-runbook and migration notes Changes made (high level): 1) terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane: main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, rg-based state locking support, tags, and example usage. 2) terraform/modules/interface-endpoints: consolidated endpoints, IAM role wiring for cross-account accepts. 3) terraform/environments/installer: wiring for multi-account scenarios and example workspace. 4) helm/private-installer: values.yaml additions, templates/peering.yaml, templates/endpoints.yaml, templates/sg.yaml 5) scripts/upgrade-hooks: add pre-upgrade snapshot and post-upgrade validation/rollback helpers. 6) tests/integration: vpc_provisioning_test.go and a small Python infra harness to validate endpoints and DNS. Backwards compatibility and upgrade notes: - Module is idempotent; existing installations without the module are unaffected until operator runs the new installer chart. - Upgrade hook takes a snapshot of current route tables and SGs; rollback restores previous state where possible. - For cross-account peering the acceptor role must be pre-provisioned in the remote account OR the operator can use the new documented manual acceptance flow. - No expected downtime for control-plane API but DNS propagation may take up to 60s for validation checks in CI. Testing: - CI runs terraform init/plan for a mocked backend and runs the integration tests in a sandbox account. - Initial CI run flagged a lint failure for a missing tag; fixed in second commit and all checks passed. Security considerations: - Endpoints default to private DNS disabled for ECR Docker unless explicitly enabled by operator. - KMS endpoint and S3 gateway are opt-in via values to reduce blast radius. Related work: Linear ENG-4321 tracks multi-az private installer improvements; SUP-1189 documents a customer support case that required peering automation. Merge notes: Squash merge after final approval. See release notes below for operator-facing steps.

release_notes: Add a reusable terraform module to provision VPC control-plane resources (subnets, interface endpoints, security groups)
Support for cross-account VPC peering with automated route updates and optional acceptor role
Route53 private hosted zone creation and peering automation with validation job
Helm values and templates for private-installer to consume provisioned network resources
Upgrade/rollback hooks to snapshot/fallback network state during installer upgrades
notes_for_operators: Before running the installer with the new module, ensure remote account acceptor role exists if you expect automated peering acceptance.
Set values.privateInstaller.network.kms_endpoint and s3_gateway to true only if your compliance team has approved managed endpoints.
Run 'helm upgrade --install --wait' and monitor installer logs for the DNS validation job. See docs/operator/vpc_control_plane.md for step-by-step.
